title: Pulsar: `msgBacklog` was the wrong name for `msgBacklogThreshold`

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **Pulsar Scaler**: Fix `msgBacklogThreshold` field being named wrongly as `msgBacklog` (#4681)
remediation: Rename `msgBacklog` to `msgBacklogThreshold` on each pulsar trigger named. 2.11.2 accepts both; 2.16 drops `msgBacklog` and the trigger silently falls back to the default threshold of 10. Rename only once the operator runs 2.11.2 or later: 2.11.0 and 2.11.1 read `msgBacklog` only and ignore `msgBacklogThreshold`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "pulsar") and (.metadata // {} | has("msgBacklog"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row still uses the old key

title: The Metrics Server's Prometheus metrics endpoint is removed

detection.reason: which endpoint a Prometheus scrape config, ServiceMonitor or dashboard reads is not in the collected projection

quote: **General**: Metrics Adapter: remove deprecated Prometheus Metrics and non-gRPC code (#3930)
remediation: Point every scrape config, ServiceMonitor and dashboard at the operator's metrics endpoint (keda-operator, port 8080, `/metrics`). The adapter's `keda_metrics_adapter_*` series were RENAMED to `keda_*` on the operator, not moved as-is, so alerts and recording rules need the new names. v2.11.0 shipped this removal (4ae8975af); the changelog bullet was filed under Improvements first and under Breaking Changes later.
verifyCommand: kubectl get servicemonitors.monitoring.coreos.com,podmonitors.monitoring.coreos.com -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("keda")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a KEDA scrape target; one aimed at the metrics server stops returning data

title: Azure Data Explorer: `clientSecret` in trigger metadata is deprecated

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

remediation: Move the secret out of the trigger metadata on each azure-data-explorer trigger named into a TriggerAuthentication `secretTargetRef` for `clientSecret` (not `clientSecretFromEnv`: 2.20 removes that too). 2.13 stops reading the metadata key and the trigger then fails to authenticate.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "azure-data-explorer") and (.metadata // {} | has("clientSecret"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row still carries the secret in metadata

title: Admission webhook rejects a ScaledObject with only cpu/memory triggers and `minReplicaCount` unset or 0

detection.reason: the condition is a conjunction — every trigger is cpu or memory AND minReplicaCount is 0 — that no single rule predicate expresses

quote: scaledobject has only cpu/memory triggers AND minReplica is 0 (scale to zero doesn't work in this case)
remediation: On each ScaledObject named, either set `minReplicaCount` to 1 or more, or add a non-resource trigger: the webhook (scaledobject_webhook.go v2.11.0:290) rejects `minReplicaCount == nil` as well as 0 when every trigger is cpu or memory — a resource-only object with no minReplicaCount at all is the common case. A ScaledObject whose triggers are all cpu/memory cannot scale to zero (there is no pod to measure), and from 2.11 the webhook rejects such an object on its next update. For each candidate named, either set `minReplicaCount` to 1 or more, or add a non-resource trigger that can activate from zero.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.minReplicaCount // 0) == 0 and ([.spec.triggers[]? | .type] | length) != 0 and ([.spec.triggers[]? | .type] | all(. == "cpu" or . == "memory"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is rejected by the 2.11 webhook on its next update
